Peripheral

puh-RIF-uh-rul — contains 'peri,' meaning around; peripheral things sit around the edge, not the center. · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Peripheral is located on the edge of something, or of only minor importance.

The report focused on the main budget crisis and treated the parking complaints as a peripheral concern.

Worked Example

A team spends an entire meeting debating which font to use on a flyer, while the event itself — the date, the venue, the guest list — barely gets discussed at all.

Spending time on a minor detail while the truly important matters get ignored shows exactly what 'peripheral' means — something on the edge, not the center, of importance. Unlike 'irrelevant,' which means it doesn't matter at all, peripheral means it matters, just far less than the main issue.

How Peripheral Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

secondary

secondary: of less importance than the main thing

minor

minor: not very important or serious

tangential

tangential: only slightly related to the main subject

Antonyms

central

central: of the greatest importance; at the core

essential

essential: absolutely necessary; of the utmost importance

How Strong Is It? — minor → irrelevant → peripheral

minor vs. peripheral

minor vs. peripheral: Minor is a plainer, weaker word than peripheral — minor just means small in importance, while peripheral specifically suggests sitting off to the side of the real, central issue.

irrelevant vs. peripheral

irrelevant vs. peripheral: Irrelevant is stronger than peripheral: something peripheral still matters a little, but something irrelevant has no bearing on the matter at all.

Build the Word

The pieces

prefix — peri-

prefix — peri-: around (Greek)

root — -pher-

root — -pher-: to carry, to bear (Greek)

suffix — -al

suffix — -al: relating to (Latin)

Put it together

Put it together: Greek periphereia ('circumference') combined peri- (around) with pherein (to carry, to bear). Something peripheral sits carried around the outer edge, not at the center.

Use the root in a new word: periscope

Use the root in a new word: periscope: The submarine crew used the periscope to see around the surface of the water without surfacing.
